claim: The installed Syzygy app can explicitly register its exact local MCP server or app-owned authenticated LAN attachment in Codex without repository script paths, while preserving unrelated Codex TOML and requiring only one host restart after a change.
commands: npm --prefix frontend exec vitest run src/components/LanAgentSettings.ui.test.ts src/components/McpSetupModal.ui.test.ts
falsifiers: A Codex restart is still required after an MCP configuration change because the host loads configured servers at startup.
This evidence does not substitute for the physical two-install Drive/LAN convergence run; that begins after both installed apps are updated and the restarted Codex task exposes syzygy-lan tools.
The LAN attachment requires Node.js because the current encrypted coordinator protocol is implemented by the embedded Node runtime scripts.

Ordinary local MCP writes remain approval-gated. The explicit paired LAN developer connection authorizes its test tools, but grants no ambient filesystem, model, credential, or human-identity authority beyond the native Syzygy tool contracts.
